summary.text: Phil Olaleye is a Democratic state representative from Georgia House District 59 who has served since 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A nonprofit executive, he is the executive director of Next Generation Men & Women and a former U.S. Peace Corps volunteer.

paragraphs.text: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, he said he graduated from Duke University in 2007 and received a master's in public policy from the Harvard Kennedy School of Government in 2014, and that he was raised in Stone Mountain, Georgia.

He said he served as director of performance management at WorkSource Atlanta and as a Peace Corps volunteer in the Philippines before becoming executive director of Next Generation Men & Women, an education nonprofit serving Atlanta high school students.
He has also served as president of Organized Neighbors of Summerhill.
Olaleye assumed office in the Georgia House on January 9, 2023, and advanced from the Democratic primary on May 19, 2026.
For 2025-2026 he was assigned to the Education Committee, the Governmental Affairs Committee and the Information and Audits Committee.
His 2022 survey listed three campaign messages: fostering thriving families, building healthy communities and defending democracy.
